source.title: Instructional control of reinforcement learning: a behavioral and neurocomputational investigation

confidence_rationale: Strong, well-replicated behavioural result with explicit computational model comparison in a solid venue, and the mapping onto MECH-011's first assertion is unusually direct -- the manipulation IS a linguistic instruction and the dependent measure IS the reinforcement-learning update. Held below 0.85 because the study concerns instrumental reward learning with arbitrary stimuli, not ethical learning or anything resembling REE's residue, so the extension from 'instruction biases value learning' to 'language biases ethical model update' is assumed rather than tested.
failure_signatures: Instructions continued to drive choice even after extended contradictory experience: the bias did not wash out with data. A REE linguistic channel that sets a prior on z_world cannot be assumed self-correcting simply because the agent keeps acting and observing.

The winning model located the distortion in the LEARNING RULE, not in the prior: the PFC/HC system amplified instruction-consistent outcomes and attenuated inconsistent ones. An implementation that adds language as an additive prior term, leaving the update untouched, would not reproduce this effect and would therefore not be a faithful model of the mechanism MECH-011 names.

Because the corrupted quantity is the reinforcement statistic itself, downstream monitors that read learned values (rather than raw outcomes) cannot detect the drift -- the record they audit has already been rewritten.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Participants performing a probabilistic selection task were told which stimulus had the highest (or lowest) reinforcement probability, where the instruction was in fact inaccurate. Despite sustained experience to the contrary, the instructions drove choice behaviour. Comparison of two neural-circuit models by Q-learning and Bayesian fit favoured a confirmation-bias account in which a PFC/HC system trains the striatal reinforcement system by amplifying outcomes consistent with the instruction and diminishing those that are inconsistent.
mapping.ree_translation: MECH-011's first assertion is that language 'biases priors during model update'. This is the cleanest available empirical instance of exactly that, and it sharpens the claim in a way REE should adopt: the bias is not merely a prior that subsequent evidence corrects, it is a gate on which evidence is allowed to count. That is also the concrete mechanism behind MECH-011's own hedge about 'rationalisation loops' -- the loop is closed because the verbal prior edits the very reinforcement signal that would otherwise falsify it. For a REE symbol channel this converts a vague warning into a testable design constraint: the linguistic pathway must write to the prior WITHOUT acquiring multiplicative control over the residue/prediction-error term, or the agent becomes unfalsifiable from the inside.
mapping.mapping_caveat: The domain is instrumental reward learning over arbitrary visual stimuli in healthy adults, not ethical learning and not harm. MECH-011 is a claim about ETHICAL learning specifically, and REE's residue is an affective care-marker rather than a scalar reward statistic; nothing here shows that an affective/harm channel is corruptible in the same way, and there are reasons to think interoceptive harm signals may be more instruction-resistant than abstract reward. Treating the two as interchangeable is the main over-reach risk. Separately, 'instruction' here is a single experimenter-supplied sentence delivered before learning, not the open-ended social linguistic traffic MECH-011 has in view.
mapping.source_context: Healthy adult humans; probabilistic selection / reinforcement-learning task with inaccurate verbal instruction; behavioural data with Q-learning and Bayesian model fitting plus neural circuit simulation.

confidence_components.notes: Weighted toward mapping_fidelity because MECH-011 is a mechanism_hypothesis: what matters is whether the proposed mechanism (language biasing model update) is real and how it is implemented. This paper answers both directly. transfer_risk is non-trivial because the reward-to-residue substitution is untested.
